game_identity.player_fantasy: Be the last maintenance runner carrying unstable charge from a central core to failing relays fast enough to keep the network alive.
game_identity.central_interaction: Route, recharge, carry, and transfer charge between a central core and four decaying relay beacons while choosing which live network problem to service next.

playable_loop: Move -> recharge at core -> choose upper/lower passage -> carry charge -> read changing relay urgency -> choose which relay to service -> touch beacon to transfer -> manage decay -> stabilize all four or black out -> retry

controls.move: WASD, arrow keys, or standard-mapped gamepad left stick / D-pad
controls.restart: R, Restart button, or standard-mapped gamepad Start

technology_stack: Plain HTML/CSS/JavaScript Canvas; local/offline browser; no dependencies

accepted_evidence.route_urgency_tradeoff: COMPLETED. Accepted evidence shows a nearby safer relay can own route/runner-charge advantage while a farther urgent relay owns network-recovery advantage; neither dominates both dimensions.
accepted_evidence.decision_chain: COMPLETED. Accepted evidence shows one service decision changes the next meaningful service decision under a comparable continuation policy.

accepted_evidence.adaptive_completion_characterization: COMPLETED AS DIAGNOSIS, NOT AS SUCCESS. Accepted QA PR #48 reaches a repeatable R2 > R4 > R3 > R1 non-terminal cycle under one declared state-driven policy. These results do not prove every possible policy fails; they are enough to stop broad heuristic shopping as the next direction.
